newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - UK traders buy strangles in FTSE index.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - UK traders buy strangles in FTSE index.

text.p: A string of trades in the FTSE 100 index options on Thursday reflected an expectation of increased market volatilty, dealers said.
Long strangle positions taken by traders showed their uncertainty about the next major move by the FTSE but the positions betrayed a belief that it will be an extreme move.

One of these was from a buyer of 300 September 3800 puts at 9p who also bought 300 September 4000 calls at 2p. This will make a profit at expiry if the index either falls below 3789 or it goes above 4011.
By 1340 GMT, the FTSE index was down 2.2 at 3870.5.
Another large position in the FTSE was initiated by a buyer of 500 November 3700 puts at 25p and 500 November 4000 calls at 36p.

Of next significance was some call buying in the index from traders optimistic about the market. The main deal from this category of traders included purchases of 250 October 3800 calls at 120-1/2p and 250 November 4100 calls at 12p.

Over in stock options cellular phone company Vodafone was active largely owing to the purchase of a calendar spread which involved selling 500 November 240 calls at 7p and buying 500 January 240 calls at 12p making a 5p net debit.
The deal may have been made as a means of acquiring long-term calls cheaply in Vodafone and with an expectation that the underlying shares will not move much between now and November expiry.
Elsewhere, there was a buyer of 250 February 180 calls at 35-1/2p in glass manufacturer Pilkington. The shares added 2-1/2p to 208-1/2p.
